Questions 32-35

Complete the summary below.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
groups.content:
European drone rules

Rules introduced in 2021 aim to protect the [32] of people on the ground and of aircraft. In the lowest-risk category, operators must [33] with the authorities, keep their drone within their line of [34] and fly below 120 metres. However, according to Paolo Marchetti, many [35] pilots have not followed the rules, often because they do not realise that the rules apply to them.

groups.instruction:
Questions 36-40

Match each statement with the correct person, A, B, C or D.

NB You may use any letter more than once.

A   Hannah Sykes
B   Paolo Marchetti
C   Ravi Menon
D   Lena Okafor

questions.explanation: Answer: vegetable waste Paragraph 1: mealworms 'feed on a mixture of bran and vegetable waste '.
Answer: leftover grain Paragraph 1: the larvae 'are feasting on leftover grain from a local brewery'.

questions.correctAnswer: five tonnes / 5 tonnes / 5 tons / five tons
questions.explanation: Answer: five tonnes Paragraph 2: when fully operational, the farm 'will produce up to five tonnes of insect protein every week'. 5,000 is the area in square metres.
Answer: land Paragraph 3: livestock farming 'requires vast areas of land '.
Answer: soya Paragraph 3: 'Much of the protein fed to European farm animals comes from imported soya '.
Answer: by-products Paragraph 4: insects 'are fed on by-products of the food industry... which would otherwise be thrown away'.
Answer: feed Paragraph 5: 'almost all of the farm's production is sold as animal feed '.
Answer: TRUE Paragraph 1: larvae eat ' leftover grain from a local brewery ', and paragraph 4 adds potato peelings and other by-products that would otherwise be thrown away.
Answer: NOT GIVEN Paragraph 2 says Visser 'started breeding insects in her garage' and describes the new farm, but nothing is said about who designed its equipment.
Answer: FALSE Paragraph 3: livestock needs 'vast areas of land', while ' Insects, by contrast, can be kept in stacked crates that take up very little space '.
Answer: TRUE Paragraph 6: ' insect meal is still more expensive than soya-based animal feed '.
Answer: FALSE Paragraph 6: ' European rules do not allow farmed insects to be given manure or kitchen waste that contains meat '.
Answer: NOT GIVEN Paragraph 6 mentions that companies are 'trying to win over shoppers with roasted crickets and mealworm snacks', but it does not compare how popular they are.

Answer: B Farmers saw hedges as 'an obstacle to efficient food production', removed them and cut the rest hard every year: ' Such hedges rarely flower or produce berries, and they gradually become thin and full of gaps '.
Answer: A Paragraph A: ' The value of a hedgerow depends on several factors, including its age, height, width , the variety of plants it contains and its general condition'.
Answer: C Paragraph C: wood chips are ' burned in biomass boilers, which are now used to heat farmhouses, village halls and even some rural schools '.
Answer: E Paragraph E mentions ' ash dieback, a disease caused by a fungus ' and 'Dutch elm disease'.
Answer: B Paragraph B: removing hedgerow was ' a process that farmers often called 'grubbing out' '.
Answer: B (coppicing) Paragraph E: ' Coppicing is also useful for dealing with disease. ... Cutting out infected trees removes a potential danger'.
Answer: C (trimming on a rotation) Paragraph F: ' It also spreads the work, and the cost of hiring contractors, more evenly over several years. '
Answer: C (trimming on a rotation) Paragraph F: some hedges are always uncut, so ' there are always flowers for insects in spring and berries for birds in winter somewhere on the farm'.
Answer: shelter Paragraph G: 'Piles of cut branches... provide shelter for hedgehogs and toads.'
Answer: standards Paragraph G: 'Tall trees growing within a hedge, known as standards , should be allowed to reach maturity'.
Answer: bats Paragraph G: holes in older trunks 'provide roosting sites for bats '. Owls use them for nesting, not roosting.
Answer: Blackthorn Paragraph G: ' Blackthorn , which flowers early in spring... is an important source of food for insects'.
Answer: rare Paragraph G: 'any species that are rare , such as the native black poplar, should always be kept'.
Answer: C Paragraph C: ' Governments, manufacturers and operators are increasingly working together to reduce the risks. '
Answer: F Paragraph F: ' Okafor describes her goal simply : I want the skies to be safe and open to everyone'.
Answer: A Paragraph A: drones near Gatwick ' brought flights to a halt for around 33 hours, disrupting the journeys of some 140,000 passengers '.
Answer: E Paragraph E: Okafor ' compares the situation to a busy airport ', where controllers know every plane's position to within a few metres.

Answer: B Paragraph B: researchers ' are working on methods to classify drones automatically according to their size, weight and flight pattern '. Paragraph C divides flights, not drones, into risk categories.
Answer: safety Paragraph C: 'The aim of these rules is to ensure the safety of both people on the ground and aircraft in the air.'
Answer: register Paragraph C: 'operators must register with the authorities'.
Answer: sight Paragraph C: they must 'keep their drone within their own line of sight at all times'.
Answer: recreational Marchetti: 'only around half of all recreational pilots have actually registered', often because hobby pilots don't know the rules apply to them.
Answer: C (Ravi Menon) Paragraph D: ' If every drone reported its exact location in real time, collisions would almost never happen '.
Answer: D (Lena Okafor) Paragraph F: ' I want the skies to be safe and open to everyone, for our generation and for those that come after us. '
Answer: B (Paolo Marchetti) Paragraph C: ' only around half of all recreational pilots have actually registered ', even though registration is required.
Answer: D (Lena Okafor) Paragraph F: her map shows two restricted zones for one location ' because two of the sources disagree about where the boundary lies '.
Answer: A (Hannah Sykes) Paragraph B: a single serious accident 'could set the whole industry back by years'; ' Public trust, once lost, would be very hard to win back. '
